idea-plugin.name: Phantom Database Console
idea-plugin.description: Connect to MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, H2, AWS JDBC Wrapper, Redshift, Athena, Oracle, SQL Server, SQLite, ClickHouse, Snowflake or any JDBC driver you add, and run SQL from the editor: highlighting for .sql files, Ctrl+Enter to run the statement at the caret, results in a sortable grid, and a lazily loaded schema tree. Drivers are data you can edit: each is found in the project's own dependencies, the local Gradle/Maven cache or jars you choose, and is downloaded from Maven only when you ask (Download, Test Connection). Nothing runs at startup. A data source in manual-commit mode keeps changes in an open transaction: review them in the Database Changes tool window and commit or roll them back; closing the project asks first. A result from one table with its primary key can be edited in the grid, and Compare With on a schema diffs two schemas and writes the SQL to make them match. SQL in Spring Data `@Query(nativeQuery = true)`, `@NativeQuery` and JdbcTemplate / JdbcClient strings is highlighted and completed like a console. JPA entities are checked against the data source's schema (tables and columns that do not exist, nullable columns mapped to non-null attributes), and @Table / @Column names complete from it. A data source can have a color (as in DataGrip): its consoles and .sql files get it as editor background and tab color, its tree rows and result tabs too. A console or .sql file can run in a chosen schema (catalog in MySQL), which unqualified table names in completion and checks also resolve against. The Database tree groups each schema's tables, views, routines, triggers and sequences in folders, can be filtered by name, and Navigate → Database Object (a Database tab in Search Everywhere) finds loaded tables, views, routines and columns without connecting. A data source can have several consoles (New Console), kept in Scratches and Consoles.
